beats.direction: Use the recurring witness with an on-screen disclaimer: CITY CONTEXT / NOT DAY-SPECIFIC.
beats.voice: Paris exposes the technical production of legitimacy through calendar inclusion, monumental rooms, official images, digital programmes, showrooms and archives. This chapter follows staging: Atmosphere is engineered through temporary architecture, power, light, sound, seating, cueing, safety and teardown—then edited out of the effortless final image.
beats.onScreen: Then: Paris Fashion Week is distributed across house-selected locations; the FHCM calendar specifies physical and digital formats rather than one permanent runway.

beats.direction: Animate only line reveals and state changes in the original evidence diagram.
beats.voice: Paris Fashion Week is distributed across house-selected locations; the FHCM calendar specifies physical and digital formats rather than one permanent runway. That earlier record fixes a point in time; it does not prove an inevitable progression toward the present.
beats.onScreen: Now: Municipal event rules form one public layer, but they do not disclose a named show’s lighting, power, scenic, accessibility or teardown plan.
beats.credit: Graphic © Rayven-Nikkita Collins; sources in claim ledger

beats.direction: Animate only line reveals and state changes in the original evidence diagram.
beats.voice: The distinction is material. A polished interface can survive after its workers, contracts, specifications or permission trail disappear, leaving the audience with an outcome but not its operating history.
beats.onScreen: Next: Venue contracts, permits, suppliers and technical drawings remain show-by-show reporting assignments unless a house, venue or authority publishes them.
